title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

errors: Indexing is sloppy. In the lemma the inverse is of ξ^{n−i} from H^i to H^{2n−i}. In corollary (ii) 'H^{2n−i}(X) → H^i(X) inverse of ξ^i' should read either 'inverse of ξ^{n−i}' or 'H^{n+i} → H^{n−i}'. This is a harmless slip.

Hypothesis 'stable par composantes homogènes': for the ring of algebraic correspondences this is exactly the Künneth condition C. If the corollary is meant to derive C from B, the lemma must be applied to the graded pieces generated by ξ and the u_i, which are homogeneous by construction, rather than to the full correspondence ring. The page does not make this point explicit. As written, the application to 'all algebraic correspondences' would be circular, unless 𝒜 is taken to be the subring generated by ξ, the homogeneous u_i and their transposes.
Proof only begun (induction on k = i+2j); not completed on this page.

ideas.what: Algebraicity of Λ is equivalent to algebraicity of the inverses of the hard Lefschetz isomorphisms L^{n−i}: H^i → H^{2n−i}
ideas.modern_name: Standard conjecture B(X) (Lefschetz type) and its equivalent forms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1968/69 Bombay paper) with proofs by Kleiman ('Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures', 1968)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay Colloquium 1968, publ. 1969)

ideas.what: B(X) implies algebraicity of the Künneth projectors and of the projections onto the Lefschetz primitive decomposition
ideas.modern_name: B(X) ⇒ C(X); algebraicity of the Lefschetz decomposition
ideas.where_published: Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles (1969); details in Kleiman 1968

ideas.what: Abstract formulation: any transposition-stable, homogeneous-component-stable operator ring containing ξ and partial inverses of ξ^{n−i} contains Λ and all primitive-decomposition projectors
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz (sl_2) algebra lemma; Lefschetz operator algebra generated by L and its partial inverses
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kleiman (1968), also implicit in Lefschetz-module/sl_2 arguments
ideas.where_published: Similar argument in Kleiman 1968 §1 and Kleiman 1994 'The standard conjectures'

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the well-known formal lemma behind 'B(X) ⇔ Λ algebraic ⇔ inverses of L^{n−i} algebraic, and B ⇒ C'. That result was published by Grothendieck (Bombay 1969) and proved in detail by Kleiman (1968). The abstract operator-ring phrasing is a minor stylistic variant, not new mathematics.

Line 3: '(et [?] stable [?])' appears to be a parenthetical such as '(càd total)' after 'stable par composantes homogènes'. The word underlined looks like 'total'; reading uncertain.
Margin note left of 'Alors' reads roughly '(et algébrique(s))', attached to the u_i.
'Alors 𝒜 contient L, Λ [?]': the image shows a single operator, most likely Λ (ξ = L is already assumed in 𝒜), followed by a struck-out word, then 'et les projections'.
Corollary (i) is probably 'Λ algébrique' rather than 'L algébrique', since L is always algebraic.
Corollary (ii): the reading 'Pour 1≤i≤n' is plausible ('∀ 1≤i≤n'); 'corr. alg.' is underlined.
Before 'S'il en est ainsi' there is a crossed-out mark; the following illegible word in 'sur les [?] facteurs' may be 'facteurs dimensionnels'.
